Arrowhead, do you even remember that Helldivers 2 is supposed to be FUN?

At this point, it genuinely feels like the developers are systematically destroying everything that made players fall in love with Helldivers 2 in the first place. And somehow, they keep doing it with astonishing determination.

Pointless balancing. This is a cooperative PvE shooter, not a competitive esports tournament with millions of dollars on the line. Why does every weapon that players find effective and enjoyable eventually have to be nerfed into the ground? Instead of making weaker weapons more interesting and viable, the developers repeatedly choose to ruin the ones people actually enjoy using. The result? Less variety, less excitement, and significantly less fun.

Paid content and endless nerfs. And don't even get me started on the paid Warbonds. You spend your hard-earned money on new weapons, enjoy them for approximately one update, and then the next patch comes along and turns your purchase into a glorified piece of scrap metal. What's the point of paying for new content if the developers are just going to make it practically worthless shortly afterward? Why should anyone feel encouraged to support the game financially when their purchases can lose most of their appeal overnight?

Damage, enemies, and ragdoll mechanics. Constant changes to fundamental gameplay systems that don't necessarily make the experience any better. One patch makes your weapons feel like they're shooting marshmallows. Another turns enemies into ridiculous bullet sponges. And then there's the endless ragdolling, where your character spends more time flying through the air, bouncing off rocks, and lying helplessly on the ground than actually fighting.

Where exactly is the fun in that? Where's the feeling of being an elite soldier armed to the teeth and sent into an overwhelming battlefield? Instead of intense, spectacular combat, we increasingly get a frustrating simulator of helplessness.

And perhaps the most infuriating part is the complete lack of a clear direction for the game. One update supposedly fixes something, and the next introduces several new problems. Mechanics that worked perfectly fine suddenly get reworked for no apparent reason. It feels like the developers have become so obsessed with endlessly tweaking numbers that they've completely forgotten the most important thing: THE GAME IS SUPPOSED TO BE FUN.

Difficulty is great. Chaos is part of Helldivers. Getting killed by some absurd accident can be absolutely hilarious. But there's a massive difference between entertaining chaos and frustratingly losing control of your character. There's a difference between a fair challenge and an artificially prolonged firefight against enemies that refuse to die.

STOP BALANCING THE FUN OUT OF YOUR OWN GAME!

Let weapons feel powerful. Let enemies be genuinely dangerous. Let players overcome challenges through skill, teamwork, and smart loadout choices instead of constantly forcing them to fight against the latest questionable balancing decisions.

I want to fight Terminids, Automatons, and Illuminate, not the developers themselves every time they release another patch deciding which weapons I'm allowed to have fun with this month.

And here's the greatest irony of all: Arrowhead has become the very embodiment of the so-called "Managed Democracy" they so relentlessly mock in their own game. You preach freedom, choice, and player empowerment while constantly dictating how we're supposed to play, what weapons we're allowed to enjoy, and what kind of fun is considered acceptable. You've somehow managed to become the very thing your own satire was making fun of.

Helldivers 2 doesn't need perfectly sterile, obsessively calculated balance. It needs to rediscover what made people fall in love with it in the first place: FUN.

Stop treating fun like a bug that needs to be patched out.

A Game I Love, but One That Continues to Disappoint

I genuinely love Helldivers 2. Few games have managed to capture the same sense of teamwork, chaos, humor, and sheer enjoyment. At its best, it's one of the most entertaining multiplayer experiences I've ever had, which makes its current state all the more frustrating.

Since the latest update, stability has become a serious issue, and it's increasingly difficult to overlook problems that should have been addressed long ago. What makes this worse is the lack of consistent communication from Arrowhead and the apparent inability to deliver meaningful, lasting improvements despite having had so much time to address these issues.

I understand that game development is complicated and that updates can introduce unexpected problems. However, there comes a point where patience turns into frustration. Players shouldn't have to constantly wonder whether the next update will actually improve the experience or introduce another round of technical issues.

What disappoints me most is how much potential this game has. The foundation is incredible, the community is passionate, and the gameplay is genuinely special. Yet it feels like the developers continuously struggle to maintain the quality of the experience they've created.

I don't want Helldivers 2 to fail. Quite the opposite. I want it to succeed because I genuinely love this game. But loving something doesn't mean ignoring its shortcomings, and after this much time, I think it's reasonable to expect better stability, clearer communication, and more consistent progress.

I want to recommend this game, but in its current state, I simply can't.

I absolutely loved this game, I purchased the super citizen edition the first week it came out when you had to wait for hours in queue just to get in due to how full the servers were at the time. I would have considered this one of the best games that I have ever played but after everything that I have experienced and seen from the developers I can not even bear to recommend this game to anyone that I know, as it is a shell of the game it used to be. In the beginning it was so much fun, I got to meet a lot of really kind people and play a incredibly unique game that was nothing like anything that I have ever played before and I loved every single second that I spent playing at that time. Although there were a few bugs here and there the game was really fresh and it seemed like they were working on fixing it as well. Sadly this was not the case and in fact has appeared to get worse and worse with every single update. Stratagem bouncing and the hellpod controls still have not been fixed at all and seemingly, it seems like they have not even glanced at it either. Honestly I have seen so many bugs this late into development (two, close to 3 years old already) that should have been fixed and yet there has been nothing done to at least try remediating these as well. I can not explain how many times I have seen enemies clip through the map, usually while I am on an elevated surface suddenly rise from under the floor that I am on and kill me or end up getting stuck because a massive dead bile titan or impaler corpse left an invisible, impassable hitbox that seemingly takes forever to clear. For a development team to have earned so much money from this games massive success and continuously ignore critical, game-ruining bugs is absolutely devastating to see. It is especially infuriating as a player and person who owns this game to see how miserably slow and lazy the development team that allegedly has a group to fix these problems have it get even more damaged each major update with it taking months to fix what seemingly is simple bugs that have been shown that they are able to be fixed with modder creating mods that fixed these problems incredibly quickly.

I would also like to point out the choices that this development team has made for the game which always seems to go against everything that the players want. I recall one of the first major controversies this development team had done being the fact that they nerfed some of the weapons that were deemed too powerful. As a result this made the game a lot more unfair and harder than it previously was and with the array that we had at the time when players were still learning was brutal. I would completely understand this choice if this was not a PVE game. Which I constantly have myself seeing with many of these changes because frankly, they seem incredibly outlandish from a players perspective such as making the knockback radius of a war strider's grenade even larger, which can leave you stunlocked allowing for you to die without having a chance to fight back or stun you from areas that you would think you would be safe in which is mildly infuriating. Then with the change with hive gaurds armor pen being changed to heavy pen, which on later difficulties spawn just as much as the weaker enemies have high armor penetration. This was already outrageous as you would then need to use a gun or support weapon that would to kill them while having to deal with plenty of them already. Luckily this was reverted but it still confuses me as to why someone would decide that this was best for the fun of the players. As this would have likely forced people to either try to ignore them or be stuck using the same support weapons to ensure that they can deal with them which weapon variety is already a problem for the game as a lot of weapons that you get either have too niche of a use or are just completely useless against specific enemies which often had me using the same loadout every single match because nothing would compare and made the game so much more repetitive. Additionally with a lot of the weapons or armors that are incredibly helpful or fun to use are locked by warbonds which are about 10 dollars each and after paying for the game I do find it a bit bothersome that I can never enjoy the new content without having to pay for it or grind super credits for days. Even then they have shown that they can do interesting things with these warbonds like cosmetics and balancing the game like with the ironclad democracy warbond which when worn practically just reverted the explosion knock back changes that they have, selling us the solution of the communities complaints for ten dollars. 

Ultimately after everything that I have seen in the game and with the developers ignoring the playerbase time and time again I legitimately can not recommend this game to anyone as I feel like they would not be delivered the game that was shown to them and that I once fell in love with and played for hours 2 years ago.

With the lack of communication from the studio regarding their roadmap, the ongoing issues surrounding EAC, and the frankly ridiculous number of long-standing QoL problems, I feel like leaving a negative review is one of the few ways left to make our frustrations heard.

Whether the studio actually cares is another matter entirely. At this point, it feels like they're more interested in defending their decisions than acknowledging when those decisions have made the game worse.

Don't get me wrong. I enjoy Helldivers 2. That's precisely why I'm so frustrated with it. The potential for something genuinely fantastic is right there, constantly just out of reach because of problems that have persisted for months, sometimes well over a year. I want this game to succeed, but wanting it to improve doesn't mean I should have to excuse the decisions holding it back.

I don't need to rehash every problem with the game. A quick Google search will show you plenty of them, along with countless discussions from players who've been asking for solutions for over a year.

Balancing problems, inconsistent mechanics, stratagem bouncing, hellpod steering, and a whole host of other QoL issues. These aren't obscure complaints from a handful of players. They're recurring frustrations that the community has been raising for ages.

And here's what really gets me.

Modders managed to address many of these problems themselves. Some of those fixes were vibe-coded, but they worked. They improved the experience in ways players had been requesting for months. Then came the EAC changes and additional security measures, which effectively gutted those solutions.

So we're left with a rather stupid situation. Players demonstrated that improvements were possible, only to lose access to them while the underlying problems remained.

If someone can vibe-code a functional fix over a weekend, why can't an entire professional development studio deliver a proper, supported solution within a reasonable timeframe?

I'm not pretending that implementing, testing, and maintaining changes in a live-service game is as simple as throwing together a mod. It isn't. But that doesn't excuse the lack of progress, nor does it make the community's frustration any less justified.

I don't want Helldivers 2 to fail. I want it to be the game it so clearly has the potential to become.

But until the developers demonstrate that they're willing to address these long-standing issues, rather than simply expecting players to put up with them, I can't recommend it.

And if a negative review is what it takes to make that frustration visible, then so be it.

       对于一个生活在具有浓厚团结意识和爱国热情的国家的我来说，看到真的存在“世界人民大团结”，无疑是兴奋的，我当时也迫不及待地想加入这场共同抵抗外族入侵者的宏大战斗中，只可惜在超级地球保卫战的时候我还没有足够的钱，因为我还是一名中学生，没有赚钱的能力，没能加入这场战斗也无疑是我的遗憾之一。直到后来，我老爸给我转了生活费后我第一时间购入了这款我梦寐已久的游戏，正式进入游戏后，我可以说这是我第一次对一款游戏有如此大的震撼，沉浸感特别强，一入手就上了瘾，周末打开电脑就是“为了民主！为了自由！”，我因此“戒掉”了Kards还有战争雷霆（开个玩笑）。总之，在很长一段时间里，这款游戏一直是我的心头好，我也一直有向同学推荐这款游戏。后来有一两次长时间没玩了，不过，并不是我玩腻了，而是迫于学业和谈恋爱。再后来，我顺利熬过了中考，有了充足的闲暇时间，我便又重拾起了绝地潜兵2，体验里面队友间为完成任务而捐躯赴义的无畏，体验游戏中各个战备数值搭配的战术性，体验面对大军压境的紧张......在这期间，尽管在网上看到很多人在吐槽箭头不优化BUG什么的，又即使，我也遇到过几次BUG，但这并没有阻挡我的热情，我依旧扮演着”绝地潜兵“的角色，披着马年红黄披风在战场上奔波，以保卫超级地球和全世界人类的名义向外星人开火。直到最近，情况急转直下，在上上周完成更新之后，一切都变了，我真的有被更新恶心到，开开心心的游戏变成了一次又一次的闪退和报错，尽管我在网上有搜索过应对教程，但并没有很大的实际作用，在今天本该是愉快的周末，又一次的闪退让我终于意识到也许应该说点什么了，也许从一开始一些小错误就不该被忽视吧。
       对不起，箭头（Arrowhead），是你让我不再能做一名高效完成任务的绝地潜兵，是你让更多的潜兵无法再守护那些纯真的孩童和超级地球的，也是你亲手毁掉了玩家们最后的一丝对于这款游戏的体验感和热情的。这个游戏本不该发展成现在这个样子的，Helldivers系列本来是有着极大发展潜力的。

Helldivers 2 has not changed in a meaningful way since its debut in 2024. Helldivers 2 has introduced several new premium weapon passes, a new faction and a handful of new biomes in two years of active development. Yet the core gameplay remains completely untouched. The same missions have been in the game since launch and new ones, if you can call them that are sprinkled in very rarely, often being some variation of: Big enemy structure(s), nuke it. Precious Data, Upload it. Rescue VIP(s). 

The developers of the game are not interested in adding more meaningful content. The community has been creating some of the most inspiring and relieving downloadable content since the games launch back in 2024. Rudimentary and basic functions that a junior developer could implement. Like a simple loadout function, something that has been a staple of team based games since Team Fortress 2 released in 2007. A company parented by one of the biggest giants in gaming, cannot give its starving player base quality of life. Instead they are more focused on senior development obstacles. Like patching an achievement that quite honestly, nobody would cry over, instead of fixing pressing matters like actually being able to control your characters descent from the sky. Which has been broken since year one of this game.

If you enjoy a sanbox that does not change, does not offer new content, where you will not be challenged and can expect the same, repetitive safe predictable threat level on every difficulty (Even the so called hardest difficulty in the game). Helldivers is not for you. Because the game will not launch for you to enjoy its cooked around the edges cold in the center offering. Whether it be anti-cheat or crashing that even a capable graphics card cannot handle.

Helldivers 2 has a lot alike with Payday 2, it has a lot of premium weapon packs that add content to the game, much like Payday 2. With the exception of that game having mission variety, replayability and a genuine fondness for its customers. Arrowhead has given me three new weapons every (odd) month, and a booster I will never be able to use because the main four boosters in this game are absolutely essential or you are (not hyperbole) debilitated beyond reason. Imagine having a booster slot for your person in real life. You have four slots. You have some boosters that make you run faster, maybe gain muscle quicker. But you cannot pick them because your four slots are taken up by existing, breathing, consciousness, and the ability to walk.

In Helldivers 2 it is a privilege to have all of the ammo that your gun can carry. You will not spawn in with your maximum amount of Healing items, ammunition, grenades, and support weapon ammo. Without a ship upgrade for your support weapon, the thing you can pay real world money for! Or the vestigial and burdensome booster that feels more like a tax on you for daring to play the game than a fun advantage you can bring to the table.

I would like to reiterate how ridiculous it is that you can give the developers your hard earned cash! Ontop of the entry fee! And not even get your ammunition for the gun you paid for!

Helldivers 2 has gone so far beyond the realm of reason that it is punishing you for supporting it.

Do not buy this game, do not wait for a discount, support developers who respect your wallet, time, patience, feedback, and especially your contributions to the community.
